paragraphs: Ulla, or Rav Ulla. Hyman places him in the fifth generation of the Amoraim of Eretz Israel, as in Shabbat ch. 3 halakhah 5 (compare [Yerushalmi Shabbat 13:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.13.5.2)): “R' Ulla says: they asked [supplied בעון] before R' Aha”; and in [Yerushalmi Shekalim 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.1.1.5): “R' Ulla objected before R' Mana”; and in [Shabbat 96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.96a.2) [supplied צו.]: “Ulla said: two Amoraim in the West disagree about it, R' Yosi bar Avin and R' Yosi bar Zevida” (and Hyman says it is known that they were in the fourth generation).

In Hyman’s reconstruction, at the end of the days of Abaye and Rava, when the sages of Eretz Israel went down to Babylonia, he too went down with them. This is what we find: 'When Ulla came he rested in Kalbano; Rava said to him: And where did the master rest?' etc., as cited by Hyman at Sanhedrin 43b (compare [Sanhedrin 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.63b.9)). Hyman describes him as like a colleague to Rava, as in Chullin 131a (compare [Chullin 131b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.131b.21-22)): 'Ulla was giving the priestly gifts to a priestess; Rava objected to Ulla.' Ulla said to him: 'Rabbi, from your own argument' [supplied מטונך] (and this is like 'master'). And likewise Yevamot 106 [supplied קו;, locator unresolved]; [Nazir 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.51a.2-3): 'Rava objected to him.'

And in Sanhedrin 65 [supplied סה, no amud mark], 'Rava said to him'; and Bava Kamma 11a, 'Rava said to him: what is your opinion?' In [Avodah Zarah 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.51a.12) Rava transmits in Ulla’s name [supplied נא..]. And he is mentioned in Shabbat 31a: 'Rav Ulla expounded.' And in [Kiddushin 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.31a.8): 'They asked Rav Ulla: how far does honoring father and mother extend?' etc. And in Shabbat 62b: 'Rav Ulla expounded' (according to the reading of דק״ס) 'what is the meaning of that which is written: and he said' etc.

And there, [Shabbat 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.31b.4-5), 'Rav Ulla taught' etc. And Hyman identifies him as the teacher of Rav Ashi, as in [Sanhedrin 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.28a.30), where Rav Ashi said, 'When we were at Ulla's.' And, Hyman asserts, without doubt, several statements said by Ulla were found that belong to the later Ulla. Hyman also lists Rava son of Rav Ulla (Shabbat 31); Ravina son of Rav Ulla (Beitzah 3 (compare [Beitzah 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.3b.3))); R' Bena'ah son of R' Ulla ([Pesachim 54a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.54a.13)).[^8]

notes.text: Abbreviation 'ובל״ס' rendered 'without doubt' (בלי ספק) per the contract, not 'in my opinion'.
The abbreviation 'דק״ס' is not in the acronym registry; kept in Hebrew, rendered tentatively as Dikdukei Soferim; uncertain.
Printed 'בעון', 'כי אתא עולא נח בקלבנו', and 'מטונך' are quoted Aramaic and translated approximately; 'בעון' left transliterated as uncertain.

Printed locators with semicolon (יבמות קו;, שבת לא;, ביצה ג;) and 'סנהדרין סה' without amud mark are retained literally. Bavli colon = amud b, full stop = amud a; the semicolon is unresolved. Printed 'ע״ז נא..' and 'פסחים נד..' end with a doubled full stop.

Whole source/current and earlier model notes read. Hyman owns fifth-generation designation, migration, laterUlla division, teacher and family assignments; withoutdoubt force retained with attribution. Root rejects earlier reviewer gloss byyourleave: מטונך means from YOUR OWN argument; full namedDavidsonChull131b paragraphs20–21 through132a paragraph0 confirms challenge/reply and Ulla’s proof. Supplied131a remains alongside matching131b–132a;131a nonmatch preserved. SourceKalbano/place and Rabbi/master gloss remain Hyman’s forms; no silent name normalization. Supplied semicolon locators Yev106/Shab31/Beitz3 and San65 withoutside remain unresolved/held; no invented sides. דק״ס retained visibly; all earlier notes qualified by this evidence rather than retired wholesale. References to printed/native readings in inherited notes are preserved historical claims; this root pass uses supplied digital text and named saved editions, not a fresh pixel or correction-history verification.

The three whole saved Davidson Hebrew paragraphs, Chullin 131b paragraphs 20–21 and 132a paragraph 0, and their corresponding whole English paragraphs confirm Rava’s objection to Ulla and Ulla’s response from your own argument. The supplied Rabbi address remains a quoted honorific with Hyman’s master gloss; the selected English renders it my teacher, but that is not an admitted teacher relationship. The supplied Chullin 131a locator and all unresolved semicolon, no-side, and doubled-period forms remain unchanged. The first unit’s fourth-generation parenthesis, the colleague inference, and the concluding list of sons are now expressly attributed to Hyman alongside his fifth-generation, migration, teacher and later-Ulla reconstruction. His without-doubt force is retained. Uncollated abbreviated personal titles are R', without expanding them or matching the several Ulla fathers. All five current mixed notes and all four carried original notes stay verbatim; all three source holds remain. There is no new Jerusalem Talmud, Rashi, דק״ס or printed-page collation, chronology, residence, genealogy, teacher, or authority admission, and no extra primary legal material or figures are imported.

Hyman’s printed notice (III, p. 974) gives Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:5. In the consulted Guggenheimer text, Ulla reports what they asked R’ Aha at 13:5, and in Shekalim 1:1 he raises an objection before R’ Mana. Davidson Shabbat 96a has Yosei son of Rabbi Avin and Yosei bar Zavda beside Hyman’s spellings. The print has בת בקלבנו and cites Sanhedrin 43b. At Davidson 63b Ulla stays overnight in Kalnevo and answers Rava’s question. The supplied text has נח בקלבנו. The exchange about gifts to a priest’s daughter is at Davidson Chullin 131b–132a, beside Hyman’s 131a. Ulla addresses Rava respectfully and answers from Rava’s own argument. Nazir 51a and Bava Kamma 11a also give the exchanges, and Avodah Zarah 51a has Rava speak in Ulla’s name. The exact Rava address cited at Sanhedrin 65 and the Yevamot 106 reference remain uncertain. Shabbat 31b has Rav Ulla expound and subsequently names Rava son of Rav Ulla. Davidson Shabbat 62b gives the “And he said” exposition to Rava son of Rav Ilai, with Hyman’s reported DKS reading remaining a separate witness claim. Kiddushin 31a names Rav Ulla in the parental-honor question. In Sanhedrin 28a Rav Ashi says “when we were at Ulla’s,” from which Hyman infers a teacher relationship. Named notices in Beitzah 3b and Pesachim 54a give Ravina and R’ Bena’ah with the patronymics Hyman reports, without identifying one father for the different notices. Hyman’s accounts of generations, migration, and the later Ulla remain his conclusions.

The consulted Yerushalmi locates Ulla’s report before Rabbi Acha at Shabbat 13:5. In Avodah Zarah 51a, Rava transmits in Ulla’s name. The links to Sanhedrin 63b and Chullin 131b–132a give the corresponding passages beside Hyman’s 43b and 131a. Hyman’s generation and namesake distinctions remain his. See also [Chullin 132a continuation](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.132a.1).
